thesis: Broaden exposure to people and ideas when the right opportunity is not yet known.
summary: Surface-area mode contrasts isolated focus with scouting relationships and opportunities. Sanchez suggests three weekly meetings, visible small wins, a five-F relationship map, walk-and-talks, more experiments and deep learning shared publicly. She closes with a positive reframe exercise and focus over a year. Workshops and Beehiiv are promoted; she discloses investing in Beehiiv.

review_status: Codex editorial draft; complete local transcript read; claims not independently verified
synthesis_method: Direct Codex extraction from complete local transcript; exact quotations verified locally
context_and_limits: Her in-person success rates, dopamine, vitamin D, venting and positivity claims are not independently checked. Opening describes monk mode as useful for those who already know their focus, while the conclusion endorses depth; exploration and commitment are different stages. More activity is qualified by asking whether it merely exhausts her. Guarantees and workshop outcomes are marketing.
review_changes: Adds scout/operator/builder sequencing, five-F mechanics, explicit product interest and positive reframing that does not deny negative feelings.
